epithet: The blind man who came to learn
lede: The Prophet ﷺ was deep in talk with the great men of Quraysh, hoping to win them, when a blind man kept calling to him to be taught. He frowned and turned aside. Ten ayat came down about that moment — and he recited them to the people himself.

names.name: ʿAbasa
names.note: Its first word. It is also called al-Aʿmā, the Blind Man, and al-Ṣākhkhah, the Deafening Blast, after the name it gives the Day near its end (80:33).

revelation.detail: It is Makkan in the saying of all, as al-Qurṭubī puts it, and Ibn al-Jawzī records the agreement. Its occasion fixes it in the years when the call was still being made to the leaders of Quraysh one by one.
revelation.when: The early years in Makkah, when he still hoped the chiefs of Quraysh would accept

evidence.quote: سُورَةُ عَبَسَ مَكِّيَّةٌ فِي قَوْلِ الْجَمِيعِ

setting: The reasoning was sound enough, as people reason. If the heads of the clans became Muslims, their clans would follow, and the persecution of the weak would end. So when the Messenger of Allah ﷺ found himself one day in close conversation with some of them — the reports name ʿUtbah ibn Rabīʿah, Abū Jahl, and Umayyah and Ubayy, the sons of Khalaf — he gave it all his attention.

Then Ibn Umm Maktūm arrived. He was blind, a cousin of Khadījah, and one of the early Muslims; he could not see who was there or what he was interrupting. “Teach me, Messenger of Allah, some of what Allah has taught you,” he said, and said it again. The Prophet ﷺ, wishing he would wait, frowned and turned back to the others.

The blind man saw none of that. But the correction came all the same, and came in the third person at first — “He frowned and turned away” — as though sparing him the directness of it. The message is not a favour to be bestowed on the important. It is a reminder, in honoured pages, and whoever wills may take it. The one who comes to you eager and in awe has a greater claim on you than the one who thinks he needs nothing.

Afterwards the Prophet ﷺ would honour Ibn Umm Maktūm whenever he saw him. He was one of the two men who called the adhān in Madinah, and more than once the Prophet ﷺ left him in charge of the city when he rode out.

occasions.title: Ibn Umm Maktūm
occasions.text: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ was one day addressing one of the great men of Quraysh, hoping for his Islam, when Ibn Umm Maktūm — one of those who had accepted Islam early — came asking him about something, and pressed him. The Prophet ﷺ wished he would hold off for that hour; he frowned and turned from him to the other. So Allah sent down: “He frowned and turned away, because the blind man came to him.”
occasions.source: Ibn Kathīr, from more than one of the commentators. ʿĀʾishah reports it in al-Tirmidhī (3331), who called the report gharīb; al-Albānī graded its chain ṣaḥīḥ.

evidence.quote: أَنَّ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ ﷺ كَانَ يَوْمًا يخاطبُ بَعْضَ عُظَمَاءِ قُرَيْشٍ، وَقَدْ طَمع فِي إِسْلَامِهِ، فَبَيْنَمَا هُوَ يُخَاطِبُهُ وَيُنَاجِيهُ إِذْ أَقْبَلَ ابنُ أُمِّ مَكْتُومٍ-وَكَانَ مِمَّنْ أَسْلَمَ قَدِيمًا-فَجَعَلَ يَسْأَلُ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ ﷺ عَنْ شَيْءٍ وَيُلِحُّ عَلَيْهِ

aim: To show what the call of the Qurʾan really is: the honour of those who benefit from it, and the worthlessness of those who turn from it.
themes: The Day each flees the other

outline.title: The reproach
outline.summary: He frowned and turned away, because the blind man came to him. What could tell you? He might be purified, or reminded, and the reminder profit him. The one who thinks himself in no need — to him you give your attention, though it is not upon you if he is not purified. And the one who came to you striving, in awe — from him you are distracted.

outline.title: What the reminder is
outline.summary: No — it is a reminder, and whoever wills may take it to heart: in pages held in honour, exalted and kept pure, by the hands of scribes who are noble and dutiful.

outline.title: The ingratitude of man
outline.summary: Perish man — how thankless he is. From what did He create him? From a drop: He created and proportioned him, then made the way easy for him, then caused him to die and be buried; then, when He wills, He will raise him. No — he has not yet done what he was commanded.

outline.title: Let him look at his food
outline.summary: We poured down the water in torrents, then split the earth, and brought out of it grain, and grapes and herbage, olives and palms, gardens dense with trees, and fruit and pasture — provision for you and your animals.

outline.title: The Deafening Blast
outline.summary: When it comes: the Day a man flees from his brother, his mother and his father, his wife and his children — each of them, that Day, with concern enough of his own. Faces that Day bright, laughing, rejoicing; and faces with dust upon them, darkness covering them.

keyAyah.why: The question that reorders priorities: what would tell you — perhaps he would be purified. No one’s worth to the message can be read from his standing.

virtues.text: “You will be gathered barefoot, naked and uncircumcised.” A woman said: “Will we see one another’s nakedness?” He ﷺ said: “O so-and-so — ‘each one of them, that Day, will have concern enough of his own’.”

before: Al-Nāziʿāt closed with: you are only a warner to whoever fears it (79:45). ʿAbasa opens with the man who feared, and was almost passed over.
after: ʿAbasa ends with the faces of that Day. Al-Takwīr shows the Day arriving — the sun folded up, the stars falling — in twelve strokes.

notable.label: Let man look at his food
